Thus did Rama speak and Bibishana answered :-
"I will arrange for thee to reach that city in one day, 0 
Prince ! May happiness attend thee ! There is an aerisl car 
named Pushpaka that shines like the sun, which the powerful 
Ravana forcibly took from Kuvera, having overcome him in 
combat. That celestial and marvellous chariot, going everywhere 
at will, is at thy disposal, 0 Thou of unequalled prowess ! That 
car, bright as a cloud, which will transport thee to Ayodhya in 
perfect safety, is here. But if I am worthy of a boon, if thou 
dost recall any merit in me, then remain here for at least one day, 
0 Virtuous One. If thou bast any friendship for me, then remain 
here with thy brother Lakshmans and Vaidehi, thy consort. 
Having received all possible homage, 0 Rama, thou shalt 
depart. 
I have prepared those honours dictated by mine 
affection, 0 Rama, do thou enjoy them with thine innumerable 
friends and thine army also. I beg thee in all humility, out of my 
profound esteem and feeling of friendship for thee, 0 Raghava ; 
I am thy servant and therefore may llOt command thee." 
Then Rama answered Bibishana, who had spoken thus in the

to his appeal. I wish to see Ksushalya, Sumitra and the illus-
trious Ksikeyi, as also mine house, my friends, the people of the 
city and the country. Grant me leave, 0 Dear Bibishana, Thou 
hast paid me sufficient honour I Do not be angry, 0 My Friend, 
I beg of thee. 0 Foremost of the Titans, prepare the aerial car 
speedily, my task bas been accomplished, what justification is

brief.summary_1line: After the war, Vibhishana offers the celestial chariot Pushpaka and hospitality, but Rama declines to delay, eager to return to Bharata and Ayodhya.

image_candidates.scene_text: Vibhishana stands with folded palms before Rama and Lakshmana, presenting the radiant celestial chariot Pushpaka shining like the sun.
The magnificent Pushpaka aerial chariot gleams in the sky, bright as a cloud lit by sunlight, ready to carry Rama back to Ayodhya.
Rama gently refuses Vibhishana’s hospitality, speaking earnestly before gathered monkeys and titans while expressing longing to see Bharata.
